result.topic_en: A Latin addendum to §40 of Jacobi's Fundamenta nova on the limiting case |q|=1 of elliptic modular functions, giving integrated series (formulas 48–54) for log k, log k', log(2K/π), 2K/π, 2kK/π, 2k'K/π and 2√k' K/π with respect to dq/q.
result.transcription:
( [-Abschrift aus Riemann's Nachlaß-] 
 [-auf Quartblättern mit Bleistift-] )

XXVII
Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der
elliptischen Modulfunctionen.

1.

I Additamentum ad §$^{um}$ 40.
[Fundamenta nova theoriae functionum ellipticarum.]
Formulae in hoc §$^o$ propositae in eo ca-
su, ubi modulus ipsius $q$ unitatem ae-
quat, consideratione satis dignae vi-
dentur, quippe quae functiones unius
variabilis pro quovis argumenti valo-
re discontinuas praebeant [-sistant-].
Series quidem propositae magna ex
parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati
aequale non convergunt, sed integran-
do series convergentes inde derivari
possunt; itaque primo integralia for-
mularum 1 – 7 propon{+a+}mus [-exhibemus-]

48) $\int_0 (\log k - \log 4\sqrt{q}) \frac{dq}{q} = -4\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{4}\log(1+q^2) - \frac{4}{9}\log(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{16}\log(1+q^4) -$
49) $\int_0 -\log k' \frac{dq}{q} = 4\log\frac{1+q}{1-q} + \frac{4}{9}\log\frac{1+q^3}{1-q^3} + \frac{4}{25}\log\frac{1+q^5}{1-q^5}$
50) $\int_0 \log\frac{2K}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{9}\log(1+q^3) + \frac{4}{25}\log(1+q^5)$
51) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\log(1-q) + \frac{4}{3}\log(1-q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\log(1-q^5)$
$= +2i\log\frac{1-qi}{1+qi} + \frac{2i}{2}\log\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{3}\log\frac{1-q^3i}{1+q^3i}$
52) $\int_0 \frac{2kK}{\pi}\frac{dq}{q} = 4\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q}}{1-\sqrt{q}} - \frac{4}{3}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q^3}}{1-\sqrt{q^3}} + \frac{4}{5}\log\frac{1+\sqrt{q^5}}{1-\sqrt{q^5}}$
$= 4i\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q}\,i}{1+\sqrt{q}\,i} + \frac{4i}{3}\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q^3}\,i}{1+\sqrt{q^3}\,i} + \frac{4i}{5}\log\frac{1-\sqrt{q^5}\,i}{1+\sqrt{q^5}\,i}$
53) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2k'K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -4\log(1+q) + \frac{4}{3}\log(1+q^3) - \frac{4}{5}\log(1+q^5)$
$= -2i\log\frac{1-qi}{1+qi} + \frac{2i}{2}\log\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} - \frac{2i}{3}\log\frac{1-q^3i}{1+q^3i}$
54) $\int_0 \left(\frac{2\sqrt{k'}K}{\pi}-1\right)\frac{dq}{q} = -\frac{4}{2}\log(1+q^2) + \frac{4}{6}\log(1+q^6) - \frac{4}{10}\log(1+q^{10}) + \frac{4}{14}\log(1+q^{14})$
$= -\frac{2i}{2}\log\frac{1-q^2i}{1+q^2i} + \frac{2i}{4}\log\frac{1-q^4i}{1+q^4i} - \frac{2i}{6}\log\frac{1-q^6i}{1+q^6i} + \frac{2i}{8}\log\frac{1-q^8i}{1+q^8i}$

items.english: The formulas proposed in this section seem quite worthy of consideration in the case where the modulus of q equals unity, since they yield functions of one variable that are discontinuous for every value of the argument.

items.quote:
Series quidem propositae magna ex
parte pro modulo ipsius $q$ unitati
aequale non convergunt, sed integran-
do series convergentes inde derivari
possunt
items.english: The proposed series for the most part do not converge when the modulus of q equals unity, but by integrating, convergent series can be derived from them.
